cues.en: He runs on a human being. He's basically a governmental software that is instantiated in every new generation in you. So his advice is to pick someone who does this in the next generation. So if you identify with this, you are no longer a human and you don't die in the sense that what dies is only the body of the human that you run on. To kill the Dalai Lama, you would have to kill his tradition.
cues.zh: 他运行在一个人身上。他本质上是一套政权软件，在每一代新人身上被实例化。所以他的建议是在下一代中挑一个人来做这件事。如果你认同这一点，你就已经不再是一个凡人，也不会真正死去，因为死去的只是承载你运行的这具人类躯体。要消灭达赖喇嘛，你必须消灭他的传统。

cues.en: And if we look at ourselves, we realize that we are to a small part like this, most of us. So for instance, if you have children, you realize something lives on in them, or if you spark an idea in the world, something lives on, or if you identify with a society around you, because you are part that you're not just this human being. Yeah. So in a sense, you are kind of like a Dalai Lama in the sense that you, Joshua Bach, is just a collection of ideas. So like you have this.
cues.zh: 如果我们审视自己，就会发现我们大多数人在某种程度上也是这样。比如，如果你有了孩子，你会意识到自己的某些部分在他们身上延续；或者如果你在世界上启发了一个想法，它也会延续下去；或者如果你认同身边的社会，因为你是其中的一部分，你就不仅仅是这个独立的个体。是的。所以从某种意义上说，你有点像达赖喇嘛，也就是说，你，Joscha Bach，只是一组思想的集合。就像你拥有这样一个——

cues.en: operating system on which a bunch of ideas live and interact. And then once you die, some of them jump off the shape. You put it the other way. Identity is a software state. It's a construction. It's not physically real. Identity is not a physical concept. It's basically a representation of different objects on the same world line. But identity lives and dies?
cues.zh: 操作系统，上面运行着并交互着一堆想法。一旦你死去，其中一些就会跳出这艘船。换句话说，身份是一种软件状态。它是一种建构，并非物理实体。身份不是一个物理概念，它基本上只是同一世界线上不同对象的表征。但身份会经历生灭吗？

cues.en: Are you attached? What's the fundamental thing? Is it the ideas that come together to form identity or is each individual identity actually a fundamental thing? It's a representation that you can get agency over if you care. So basically you can choose what you identify with if you want to. No, but it just seems if the mind is not real, that the birth and death is not a crucial...
cues.zh: 你有执念吗？什么才是最根本的？是汇聚成身份的那些想法，还是每个个体身份本身才是根本之物？它是一种表征，只要你在意，你就可以对它拥有主导权。所以基本上，如果你愿意，你可以选择自己去认同什么。不，但感觉如果心灵不是真实的，那么生与死就不是一个至关重要的……

cues.en: part of it. Maybe I'm attached to this whole biological organism, but it seems that being a physical object in this world is an important aspect of birth and death. It feels like it has to be physical to die. It feels like simulations don't have to die.
cues.zh: 部分。也许我对整个生物有机体抱有执念，但在现实世界中作为一个物理对象，似乎是生与死的重要维度。感觉必须是物理实体才会死亡，而模拟似乎并不必然会死去。

cues.en: The physics that we experience is not the real physics. There is no color and sound in the real world. Color and sound are types of representations that you get if you want to model reality with oscillators. So colors and sound in some sense have octaves. And it's because they are represented probably with oscillators. So that's why colors form a circle.
cues.zh: 我们所体验的物理世界并不是真实的物理。真实世界中没有颜色和声音。颜色和声音只是当你试图用振荡器对现实进行建模时所获得的一类表征。所以从某种意义上说，颜色和声音都有八度音阶。这很可能是因为它们是由振荡器来表征的。这就是为什么颜色会形成一个环——

cues.en: of use and colors have harmonics sounds have harmonics as a result of synchronizing oscillators in the brain right so the world that we subjectively interact with is fundamentally the result of the representation mechanisms in our brain they are mathematically to some degree universal there are certain regularities that you can discover in the patterns and not others but the patterns that we get this is not the real world the world that we interact with is always made of too many parts to count right so
cues.zh: 色相环，而且颜色有谐波，声音也有谐波，这都是大脑中振荡器同步的结果，对吧？所以我们主观与之交互的世界，从根本上说，是我们大脑中表征机制的产物。它们在数学上具有某种程度的普适性；你可以在模式中发现某些规律，而发现不了其他规律，但我们所获得的这些模式并不是真实世界。我们与之交互的世界，其组成部分总是多到数不清，对吧？所以——

cues.en: When you look at this table and so on, it's consisting of so many molecules and atoms that you cannot count them. So you only look at the aggregate dynamics at limit dynamics. If you had almost infinitely many particles, what would be the dynamics of the table? And this is roughly what you get. So geometry that we are interacting with is the result of discovering those operators that work in the limit that you get by building an infinite series that converges.
cues.zh: 当你看着这张桌子等等时，它由无数分子和原子组成，多到你数不过来。因此你看到的只是聚合动力学，即极限动力学。如果拥有近乎无限多的粒子，这张桌子的动力学表现会是怎样？这大致就是你所感知到的东西。因此，我们与之交互的几何学，正是通过构建一个收敛的无穷级数，在极限状态下发现那些起作用的算子所得到的产物。

cues.en: for those parts where it converges its geometry, for those parts where it doesn't converge its chaos. Right. And then so all of that is filtered through the consciousness that's emergent in our narrative. So the consciousness gives it color, gives it feeling, gives it flavor. So I think the feeling, flavor and so on is given by the relationship that a feature has to all the other features.
cues.zh: 收敛的部分构成了几何，不收敛的部分则成了混沌，对吧。而所有这一切都会经由我们叙事中涌现的意识过滤。因此意识赋予了它色彩、感受和滋味。所以我觉得，感受和滋味等特质，是由某个特征与其他所有特征之间的关系所赋予的。

cues.en: It's basically a giant relational graph that is our subjective universe. The color is given by those aspects of the representation or this experiential color where you care about, where you have identifications, where something means something, where you are the inside of a feedback loop. And the dimensions of caring are basically dimensions of this motivational system that we emerge over. The meaning of the relations, the graph. Can you elaborate that a little bit? Like where does the...
cues.zh: 它基本上是一个构成我们主观世界的庞大关系图谱。而这种色彩——或者说这种体验上的色彩——是由你所在意、能产生认同、具有某种意义，或者你处于反馈回路内部的表征维度所赋予的。而在意的维度，本质上就是我们从中涌现出来的这套动机系统的各个维度。关系的意义，也就是图谱的意义。你能稍微展开讲讲吗？比如……

cues.en: Maybe we can even step back and ask the question of what is consciousness to be observed more systematically? How do you think about consciousness? I think that consciousness is largely a model of the contents of your attention. It's a mechanism that has evolved for a certain type of learning. At the moment our machine learning systems largely work by...
cues.zh: 也许我们甚至可以退一步问：要想更系统地观察，意识究竟是什么？你是怎么看待意识的？我认为意识在很大程度上就是对注意力内容的建模。它是一种为了某种特定学习方式而进化出来的机制。目前我们的机器学习系统大多是通过……

cues.en: building chains of weighted sums of real numbers with some non-linearity. And you will learn by piping an error signal through these different chained layers and adjusting the weights and these weighted sums. And you can approximate most polynomials with this if you have enough training data.
cues.zh: 构建带有非线性的实数加权和链条来运作的。你通过将误差信号输送穿过这些不同的级联层，并调整这些加权和中的权重来进行学习。只要有足够的训练数据，你就能用这种方法逼近大多数多项式。

cues.en: But the price is you need to change a lot of these weights. Basically, the arrow is piped backwards into the system until it accumulates at certain junctures in the network. And everything else evens out statistically. And only at these junctures, this is where you had the actual arrow in the network, you make the change there. This is a very slow process.
cues.zh: 但代价是你需要修改大量的权重。基本上，误差被反向传回系统中，直到它在网络的某些关键节点上累积起来。而其他部分在统计上都被平均掉了。只有在这些节点上，也就是网络中实际出现误差的地方，你才会做出调整。这是一个非常缓慢的过程。

cues.en: And our brains don't have enough time for that because we don't get old enough to play go the way that our machines learn to play go. So instead, what we do is an attention-based learning. We pinpoint the probable region in the network where we can make an improvement. And then we store this binding state together with the expected outcome in a protocol. And this ability to make indexed memories for the purpose of learning to revisit these commitments later, this requires
cues.zh: 而我们的大脑没有那么多时间，因为我们活不到能像机器学围棋那样学会下围棋的岁数。所以相反，我们采用的是基于注意力的学习。我们精确定位网络中可能可以做出改进的区域。然后将这种绑定状态与预期结果一起存储在一个协议中。而这种为了学习而建立带索引记忆、以便日后重新审视这些决策承诺的能力，需要

cues.en: and memory of the contents of our attention. Another aspect is when I construct my reality, I make mistakes. So I see things that turn out to be reflections or shadows and so on, which means I have to be able to point out which features of my perception gave rise to a present construction of reality. So the system needs to pay attention to the features that are currently in its focus.
cues.zh: 对我们注意力内容的记忆。另一个方面是，当我构建自己的现实时，我会犯错。比如我看到的东西结果只是倒影或阴影等等，这意味着我必须能够指出是我感知的哪些特征导致了当前对现实的构建。因此系统需要关注目前处于其焦点之中的那些特征。

cues.en: It also needs to pay attention to whether it pays attention itself, in part because the attentional system gets trained with the same mechanism, so it's reflexive, but also in part because your attention lapses if you don't pay attention to the attention itself. It's this thing that I'm currently seeing just a dream that my brain has spun off into some kind of daydream, or am I still paying attention to my percepts? You have to periodically go back.
cues.zh: 它还需要注意自己是否在保持专注，部分原因是注意力系统是用同样的机制训练的，所以具有自反性；但另一部分原因在于，如果你不关注注意力本身，注意力就会分散。我现在看到的这东西，只是大脑陷入某种白日梦里的幻象，还是说我仍然在关注自己的感知？你必须定期回过头来，

cues.en: and see whether you're still paying attention. And if you have this loop and you make it tight enough between the system becoming aware of the contents of its attention and the fact that it's paying attention itself and makes attention the object of its attention, I think this is the loop over which we wake up. So there's this, so there's this attentional mechanism that's somehow self-referential that's fundamental to what consciousness is. So just to ask you a question, I don't know how much you're familiar with,
cues.zh: 看看自己是否还在专注。如果你有了这样一个回路，并且把它收得足够紧——让系统既能意识到它注意的内容，又能意识到自己正在专注这一事实，并把注意力本身作为关注的对象——我认为这就是让我们“醒来”的回路。所以存在这样一个某种程度上自指的注意力机制，它是意识本质的基础。顺便问你个问题，我不知道你对这个有多熟悉，

cues.en: The recent breakthroughs in natural English processing, they use attentional mechanisms, they use something called transformers to learn patterns and sentences by allowing the network to focus its attention to particular parts of the sentence into each individual. So like, parametrize and make it learnable the dynamics of a sentence by having like a little window into the sentence.
cues.zh: 最近自然语言处理领域的突破，它们使用了注意力机制，使用了一种叫 Transformer 的东西来学习句子中的模式，方法是让网络能够把注意力集中在句子的特定部分，落实到每个个体上。就像是给句子开了一扇小窗，从而把句子的动态过程参数化并使其可学习。

cues.en: Do you think that's like a little step towards that eventually will take us to the intentional mechanisms from which consciousness can emerge? Not quite. I think it models only one aspect of attention. In the early days of automated language translation, there was an example that I found particularly funny, where somebody tried to translate a text from English into German, and it was a bat broke the window.
cues.zh: 你觉得这是不是朝着最终孕育出意识的意向机制迈出的一小步？不完全是。我认为它只模拟了注意力的一个方面。在机器自动翻译的早期，有一个我觉得特别好笑的例子，有人尝试把一段英文翻译成德文，原文是“a bat broke the window”（一只蝙蝠撞碎了窗户/一根球棒砸碎了窗户）。

cues.en: And the translation in German was... So to translate back into English, a bat, this flying mammal, broke the window with a baseball bat. And it seemed to be the most similar to this program because it somehow maximized...
cues.zh: 而德语翻译出来的意思是……翻回英语就是：一只蝙蝠，也就是那种会飞的哺乳动物，用一根棒球棒砸碎了窗户。在这个程序看来，这似乎是最贴切的，因为它在某种程度上最大化了……

cues.en: the possibility of translating the concept bad into German in the same sentence. And this is a mistake that the transformer model is not doing because it's tracking identity. And the attentional mechanism in the transformer model is basically putting its finger on individual concepts and make sure that these concepts pop up later in the text and tracks basically the individuals through the text. And it's why
cues.zh: 在同一个句子里把 bat 这个概念翻译成德语的可能性。而这正是 Transformer 模型不会犯的错误，因为它在追踪同一性。Transformer 模型中的注意力机制，基本上就是把手指按在具体的概念上，确保这些概念在后文中出现，并在整个文本中追踪这些个体。这也是为什么

cues.en: The system can learn things that other systems couldn't before it, which makes it, for instance, possible to write a text where it talks about the scientist, then the scientist has a name and has a pronoun, and it gets a consistent story about that thing. What it does not do, it doesn't fully integrate this. So this meaning falls apart at some point. It loses track of this context. It does not yet understand that everything that it says has to refer to the same universe. And this is where this thing falls apart.
cues.zh: 该系统能学到以前系统学不会的东西，比如让它能写出一篇先提到某位科学家、然后这位科学家有了名字和代词、并围绕其展开连贯故事的文本。但它做不到的是，它无法将这些完全整合起来。所以这种意义在某一刻会崩塌。它会跟丢这个上下文。它还不明白自己所说的一切都必须指向同一个世界。而这正是它破功的地方。

cues.en: But the attention in the transformer model does not go beyond tracking identity. And tracking identity is an important part of attention, but it's a different, very specific, attentional mechanism. And it's not the one that gives rise to the type of consciousness that we have. Just to link on, what do you mean by identity in the context of language? So, when you talk about language, you have different words that can refer to the same concept. Got it. And in the sense that... It's a space of concepts.
cues.zh: 但 Transformer 模型中的注意力机制，充其量只是在追踪同一性。追踪同一性固然是注意力的重要组成部分，但它是一种截然不同且非常特殊的注意力机制。它并不能催生出人类所拥有的那种意识。顺着这个话题，你在语言语境下说的“同一性”具体是指什么？这么说吧，在语言中，不同的词可以指向同一个概念。明白了。从某种意义上说……它是一个概念空间。

cues.en: So yes, and it can also be in a nominal sense or in an ethical sense that you say this word does not only refer to this class of objects, but it refers to a definite object to some kind of agent that waves their way through the story and is only referred by different ways in the language. So the language is basically a projection from a conceptual representation from a scene that is evolving.
cues.zh: 没错，而且它也可以是在指称意义上，或者伦理意义上，即某个词不仅指代这一类物体，还指代一个特定的对象，比如在故事中穿针引线的某个主体，只是在语言中用不同的方式被指代而已。因此，语言本质上是将不断演化的场景中的概念表征，

cues.en: into a discrete string of symbols. And what the transformer is able to do, it learns aspects of this projection mechanism that other models couldn't learn. cues.zh: 投影成一串离散的符号序列。而 Transformer 的过人之处在于，它学会了这种投影机制中其他模型无法掌握的方面。那么你是否见过某种人工智能，或者任何不同于神经网络、亦或存在于神经网络之中的构建构想，能够形成这样一种系统，在其中

cues.en: the space of concepts continues to be integrated. So what you're describing, building a knowledge base, building this consistent larger and larger sets of ideas that would then allow for a deeper understanding. Wittgenstein thought that we can build everything from language, from basically a logical grammatical construct. And I think to some degree, this was also what Minsky believed. So that's why he focused so much on common sense reasoning and so on.
cues.zh: 概念空间能够持续地融合？也就是说，构建一个知识库，构建起这种越来越大、高度自洽的思想集合，从而实现更深层的理解。维特根斯坦曾认为，我们可以从语言出发构建一切，本质上就是从逻辑语法的构建出发。我认为在某种程度上，明斯基也是这么相信的。所以他才会如此专注于常识推理等领域。

That's true, but- And out Psych is a productive project. It's just probably not one that is going to converge to general intelligence. The thing that Wittgenstein couldn't solve, and he looked at this in his book at the end of his life, Philosophical Investigations, was the notion of images.
cues.zh: 受他启发的项目之一就是 Cyc。它基本上——那个项目现在还在做。是的。当然，思想是不会消亡的。消亡的只有人。确实，但是——而且 Cyc 是个富有成果的项目。只是它大概无法收敛到通用人工智能。维特根斯坦无法解决的问题——他在晚年的著作《哲学研究》中探讨过这个问题——就是“图像”的概念。

cues.en: So images play an important role in Tractatus, the Tractatus attempt to basically turn philosophy into logical probing language, to design a logical language in which you can do actual philosophy that's rich enough for doing this. cues.zh: 图像在《逻辑哲学论》中扮演着重要角色，《逻辑哲学论》试图将哲学转化为一种用逻辑探索的语言，设计出一种足够丰富、能用来真正做哲学的逻辑语言。而难点在于如何处理知觉内容。最终，我认为他意识到自己无法解决这个问题。

cues.en: And I think this preempted the failure of the logitist program in AI and the solution as we see it today is we need more general function approximation. There are functions, geometric functions that we learn to approximate that cannot be efficiently expressed and computed in a grammatical language. cues.zh: 我认为这预示了人工智能中逻辑主义路线的失败，而我们今天看到的解决方案，是需要更通用的函数逼近。有些我们学会去逼近的几何函数，是无法在语法语言中被高效表达和计算的。当然，我们可以构建自动机，通过数论等方法在代数中学习，然后计算出这种几何的近似值。但是

So functional, where you kind of just said that neural networks are sort of, the approach that neural networks takes is actually more general than what can be expressed through language. Yes. So what can be efficiently expressed through language at the data rates at which we process grammatical language? Okay, so you don't think so. You don't think the language is
cues.zh: 将语言和几何等同起来并不是一种高效的思考方式。所以从泛函的角度，你刚才的意思是，神经网络所采用的方法，实际上比通过语言所能表达的更为通用。是的。也就是比在处理语法语言的数据速率下所能高效表达的更为通用。好的，所以你不认同。你不认为语言是……

But language is not fundamental to cognition and intelligence and consciousness. So I think that language is a particular way.
cues.zh: 所以你不同意维特根斯坦的观点，认为语言也不是最根本的。我同意维特根斯坦的观点。只是我认同的是后期的维特根斯坦。同时我也赞赏前期维特根斯坦的思想之美。我认为《逻辑哲学论》本身大概是20世纪写得最美的一部哲学著作。但语言并不是认知、智能和意识的基石。因此我认为，语言只是一种特殊的方式。
